referents.why: 'your staff' is second masculine singular; the one told to stretch out the staff is Aaron (w7).
The implied 'you' of 'say to Aaron' is the one the LORD speaks to, Moses (w4). Aaron is the object of the saying, not its speaker.
referents.category: implied subject of a saying command

referents.why: Inside the commanded speech the imperatives are addressed to Aaron; second masculine singular is Aaron.
Same speech; the command to strike is addressed to Aaron.
Third masculine singular weqatal after the strike: the thing struck, the dust (w15), is what will become gnats. The act decides, not the nearest noun.
referents.category: implied subject from the object acted on

links.why: Reversed and cross-verse: cl0 opens the verse as a wayyiqtol continuing the previous verse, and a within-verse then cannot run from the later strike back to it.
Two imperatives of one person joined by waw: plain and.
An imperative then waw plus a third-person weqatal saying what will come of it is a result, not a then.
Striking the dust is the act whose outcome is the dust becoming gnats; cl4 is the effect of the imperative group.
cl0 is the LORD speaking to Moses; cl1 'Tell Aaron' is the said clause.
cl1 is a saying whose content is a run of commands joined by and (stretch out, strike), so the content is the whole imperative group.
links.category: speech content of a collection of commands

groups.why: The LORD speaks to Moses. The commanded speech to Aaron is nested as a part, rather than its clauses being parts of the LORD's turn.
Moses is the one commanded to speak, so he is the sender of the words to Aaron (R2). The builder gave the sender as the implied you of cl1, which is a slot, not a candidate.
Stretch out and strike are commands joined by and at one level: one imperative group, with the weqatal as its effect.
Merged into imp2: commands joined by and at one level form one imperative group, and part is not a role of that kind.
